findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment can lose updates
findings.body: The retryCount is updated via `data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 }`, using the value read earlier in the same request rather than Prisma's atomic `increment` operator. If the cron endpoint is ever invoked concurrently (e.g. overlapping schedules, retried HTTP calls, or multiple workers), two requests reading the same reminder's retryCount at the same time will both write retryCount+1 based on the stale value, causing one increment to be lost. Since the cleanup logic in this same PR deletes reminders once retryCount > 1, undercounting means a persistently-failing reminder (e.g., due to an invalid phone number) may never reach the deletion threshold and keep being retried indefinitely, defeating the purpose of this fix. Use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } } }` instead.

findings.title: Broad delete condition not scoped to SMS method
findings.body: The deleteMany OR clause's second branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, unlike the first branch. retryCount is a generic column on WorkflowReminder used for all methods (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), and currently only this SMS cron sets it, but that is an implicit assumption, not enforced by the schema or query. If any other code path (now or in the future) increments retryCount on an EMAIL or WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder, this query will silently delete those reminders as well, even though they were never scheduled for SMS. This is a landmine that could cause silent loss of unrelated workflow reminders. The retryCount branch should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to match intent.

findings.title: Outdated comment does not describe new deletion criteria
findings.body: The comment above the deleteMany call still reads "delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date", but the query was extended to also delete any WorkflowReminder (regardless of method/scheduled state) once retryCount > 1. The comment should be updated to mention the retry-based deletion so future maintainers understand both deletion conditions.

findings.title: No automated tests added for new retry/delete behavior
findings.body: This PR introduces new business logic (retryCount increments on failure, and deletion once retryCount exceeds 1) but adds no unit or integration tests verifying: that retryCount increments correctly on scheduling failure and on thrown errors, that reminders are deleted after the threshold is reached, and that the scoping of the delete query behaves as expected. Given this handles data deletion, lack of test coverage increases risk of regressions going unnoticed.
